claim: The documented supersonic entry threshold is 2200 uu/s while the maximum car speed is 2300 uu/s. Boost-active duration above the threshold is a different observation from threshold uptime, and neither proves waste or decision quality.
limitations: The article records a June 30 rollback of its changed collision checks. Use only the explicitly unchanged threshold facts; do not assert exact current collision behavior or reconstruct the game state from speed alone.
counterexamples: Boost may accelerate above entry threshold; steering or aerial redirection needs contextual review.
practical_cue: Inspect the purpose of the boost interval before considering a different action.

claim: The RLBot community values reference reports that a small pad gives 12 boost. This does not establish a universal boost target or the availability of a pad in a replay.
limitations: AntiRL does not currently observe pad pickup/cooldown state. Decorative pad glow is not evidence of availability or collection. Map locations can vary.
counterexamples: A convenient route can be unsafe under pressure or the pad can be empty.
practical_cue: Practise a recovery route in freeplay, then review whether that route preserved your position in a same-mode match.

claim: Miao et al. studied cognitive differences between esports experts and amateurs. The study does not supply Rocket League promotion timelines, calibrated player grades, or proof that a particular drill causes rank gains.
evidence_type: meta-analysis; not a Rocket League longitudinal cohort
limitations: No comparable longitudinal Rocket League dataset or forecast calibration was supplied. Abstain from grades and timelines.
counterexamples: Players with similar ranks and weekly hours can have different learning histories and match conditions.
practical_cue: Offer an optional practice block and a same-mode replay review checkpoint, not a promotion date.
